description.narrative:
The Nexus Platform Steering Committee is the Nexus consortium’s governing board. The Steering Committee leads and oversees the strategic direction of the Nexus platform.
Pillar 1: Investing in Institutional Strengthening Immediate outcome 1: Nexus members have integrated Enterprise Resource Planning systems for HR, finance, logistics and procurement contributing to financial accountability for efficient and effective, locally-led delivery of programming.
This project will strengthen institutional capacity of NEXUS members by investing in organizations’ digital ERP, integrating finance, human resources and logistics systems. Starting from a review and audit of NEXUS member organizations’ systems, each NEXUS member will be able to invest in the required upgrade as per identified gaps. Strengthened systems are a key component of institutional capacity, improving financial accountability and allowing for stronger qualitycontrol checks, increased absorption capacity, high-quality project implementationand timely reporting. A total investment of EUR 583,000 for eight organizations over 4 years, co-funded by the Embassy of The Netherlands and Swiss Development Corporation(SDC), complements current organizational development interventions under DRA. Thistotal amount is calculated based on an amount of EUR 70,000 per organization (based on the average the NEXUS members received from their suppliers after consulting them). The exact amount needed per organization will be determined after completion of the system’s audit.
Pillar 2: Community-Driven Development with Government and Private Sector Partners Immediate outcome 2: Nexus members have a tested approach for community-driven development with government and private sector partners. The Community-Driven Development (CDD) model supports community-prioritized interventions to improve livelihoods and build demand and capacity for local level development at community level. NEXUS’ locally-led CDD modelis unique in its triple nexus approach, integrating humanitarian, development and peacebuilding interventions. As part of the proposed project, NEXUS will undertake three pilot CDD projects in Jubaland (Afmadow District), Galmudug (Adado District) and Somaliland(El Af Weyn District). These are locations where NEXUS members have existing presence. The CDD process and projects will be implemented over the course of 4 years

participating-org.narrative:
Nexus is a unique consortium, led by eight pioneering Somali NGOs, aspiring to advance a locally driven agenda for change by building partnerships between communities, civil society and the public and private sectors as well as through the implementationof integrated and sustainable interventions across the triple nexus of humanitarian, peace and development.
Founded in 2019, Nexus is a paradigm-shifting platform comprising of Eight core members: • Centre for Peace and Democracy (CPD) • Gargaar Relief and Development Organization (GREDO) • Horn of Africa Voluntary Youth Committee (HAVOYOCCO) • KAALO • Save Somali Women and Children (SSWC) • Social-Life and Agriculture Development Organization (SADO) • Taakulo Somaliland Community (TASCO) • Wajir South Development Association (WASDA)
The eight NEXUS member organizations bring to the table rich and incredibly diverse strengths and qualities that makes the platform stronger and grow exponentially going forward. Their extensive expertise and experience across varying thematic areas, and their relationships and rapport amongst one other is the most significant qualities that enriches the platform to achieve its strategic objectives. The organizations’ presence in all the regions in Somalia/Somaliland and their decades of involvement in humanitarian interventions make them a strong force in Somalia’s ever evolving and highly competitive humanitarian space.
Nexus core members possess wide-ranging technical capacities and represent communitiesacross all Federal Member States of Somalia and Somaliland. Nexus alsohas two international partners who are committed to the localization agenda – Oxfam and Save the Children
The members have been implementing humanitarian, development and conflict prevention, mitigation and response programs amidst relative calm, conflict and during disasters (both natural and man-made). It is the experience that gives the members the confidence and agility to continue working for such a long time. Nexus’ approach isambitious but is grounded in the widely recognized need for more dynamic interventions tothe chronic challenges faced by Somalia and Somaliland.
